name: Permutations
whenToUse: Choose $k$ items from $n$ where ORDER matters: rankings, officer roles, arranging people in a row.
example: A president, vice president and secretary can be chosen from $10$ people in $10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 = 720$ ways. All $6$ books on a shelf can be arranged in $6! = 720$ ways too.
pitfall: If the roles are identical (a committee instead of officers), order does not matter and you must divide by $k!$, giving a combination.
